title: Fedbank Financial Services Ltd - 544027 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Fedbank Q4 FY26 PAT rose 40% YoY to INR100.5 crore, with AUM at INR20,153 crore (+27%) and gold AUM up 76%.
summary.overview: Fedbank crossed INR100 crore quarterly PAT for the first time, with ROA of 2.6% and ROE of 14%. Growth was led by gold loans, where disbursals hit INR10,744 crore in Q4 and gold AUM reached INR10,352 crore. Asset quality improved sequentially, with GNPA at 1.9% (from 2.1% in Q3) and credit cost at 0.7% in Q4 and 0.8% for FY26. CRAR rose to 22.4% after a INR450 crore subordinated debt raise and secured-book sales, despite leverage rising to 4.6x.

financial_highlights.value: Growth not quantified in absolute terms

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursals INR10,744 crore (+37% QoQ, +135% YoY); AUM INR10,352 crore (+76% YoY). Doorstep gold AUM INR1,730 crore (+108% YoY, about 17% of AUM). Average AUM per branch INR16.5 crore after 148 new branches in FY26.

segments.name: Small ticket LAP (ST LAP)
segments.commentary: FY26 disbursals INR904 crore; Q4 INR289 crore (+39% QoQ). Book about INR3,800 crore. Management says collections were verticalised and collection staff roughly doubled; credit cost was a key drag in FY25.

segments.name: Medium ticket LAP (MT LAP)
segments.commentary: FY26 disbursals INR2,180 crore; Q4 INR632 crore (+16% QoQ). Management says yields have held.

segments.name: Business loans (unsecured)
segments.commentary: Entire INR886 crore book was assigned in Q1 and Q2 FY26, derecognised from AUM; secured book now above 99.5% of on-book AUM.

segments.name: Co-lending (CLM)
segments.commentary: Book about INR2,100 crore (21% of total book) at AUM-level spread of about 4%. Gold co-lending rose INR1,131 crore to INR2,127 crore in the year.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance of 20-25% for the company, reiterated for FY27.
Gold: budgeted on 10-15% tonnage growth; flat gold prices could still deliver about 20-22% gold AUM growth.
FY27 credit cost to stay range-bound; ROA targeted to expand 20-30 bps over FY26 average, to come from opex and/or credit cost.
Fee income expected to reach 0.8-1% of total assets in the ROTA tree, as LAP disbursals recover and business loan fees drop out of the base.
Gold yields expected to recover in Q1 FY27 towards Q2 FY26 levels if competition stays steady; LAP yields expected to hold.
Management expects to continue opening gold branches in FY27 and reduce reliance on DA income.
capex_capacity: 148 new gold branches opened in FY26, with 34 in Q4; further branch expansion planned in FY27.
70 ST LAP branches co-located with gold branches in FY26, releasing ST LAP premises.
Management says each branch can hold INR60-65 crore of portfolio, limited by locker/safe-room capacity; FY25 branches average about INR20 crore AUM.
Raised about $250 million in ECB to date; INR450 crore subordinated debt raised in Q4.
demand_pricing: Gold yields fell about 12 bps YoY (optically 28 bps) on back-ended disbursals and a 5-10 bps deliberate pricing cut in Q4; management says competition has not yet hit its branch catchments.
Gold average ticket size rose from INR1.5 lakh to about INR2.6-2.7 lakh, largely due to gold price increases; expected to flatten if prices stabilise.
Active gold customers above 3 lakh (up 17% YoY); about 60,000 new customers added in Q4, about half from new branches.

New RBI-linked assessment regime from 1 April 2026: exposure above INR2.5 lakh requires income/cash-flow assessment; management expects impact to settle within about a month. LTV limits: 85% up to INR2.5 lakh, 80% up to INR5 lakh, 75% above INR5 lakh; about 90% of book is below 75% LTV, so no provisioning impact is expected from margin breaches.
Fee income fell YoY due to lower LAP disbursals and absence of business-loan fees.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gold yields soften in the last two quarters, and is origination yield under pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 5-10 bps to deliberate pricing and the rest to back-ended disbursals. Origination pressure is seasonal, and Q1 should recover; competition has not yet entered the company's catchments.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new LTV and margin rules raise NPAs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a margin breach does not require provisioning or NPA classification; only margin calls are triggered. About 90% of the book is below 75% LTV.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ST LAP business profitable and will it grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to say if the INR3,800 crore book is currently profitable, and said it expects a better answer in about a year. ST LAP growth is expected to track the market, with internal issues described as resolved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 ROA and credit cost path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets ROA up 20-30 bps over FY26 in FY27, through opex or credit cost, with a similar path in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Gold AUM per branch and peer comparison?
qa_highlights.answer: Average AUM per branch is INR16.2-16.5 crore overall; branches open before FY25 average about INR20 crore. Capacity is INR60-65 crore per branch.

qa_highlights.question: How is April 2026 for asset quality and collections?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no stress is visible yet from the customer side; stress is expected to show up later in the affordable segment with a lag.

risks_watch: Gold yield recovery in Q1 FY27 depends on competitive intensity in gold lending.
ST LAP book (about INR3,800 crore) is still not confirmed as profitable; disbursals are about INR290-300 crore per quarter.
Higher borrowing costs: about 25% of borrowings are fixed (30-35% including commercial paper). Leverage rose to 4.6x and the company built liquidity amid Gulf geopolitical volatility.
Gold price risk: management says flat prices still allow 20-22% gold AUM growth, but a 10-15% fall would test growth and ticket size.
Lagged industry stress in the affordable segment may show up later in FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on gold growth, asset quality and ST LAP recovery, but cautious on the rate and geopolitical outlook. Management declined to give ST LAP profitability and FY27 guidance beyond ranges, and gave no figures on mortgage slippages by segment.
key_quotes: So we are at par with the market as we speak.

And we take price as a bonus.
So right now, we are not seeing anything from the customer side.

adds.what: 148 new gold branches opened in FY26 (34 in Q4); further gold branch expansion planned in FY27
70 ST LAP branches co-located with gold branches in FY26 (releases ST LAP premises, not new capacity)

growth.why: Management reiterated 20-25% AUM growth for FY27 (held), plus new guidance of 20-30 bps ROA expansion, backed by 148 new gold branches opened in FY26 and gold disbursals up 135% YoY, with gold tonnage budgeted at 10-15% growth; no order-book or hard capacity numbers for FY27 branch additions were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: FY27, with gold yield recovery in Q1 FY27
rows.why: Management targets ROA up 20-30 bps over FY26 average in FY27 from opex and/or credit cost, and expects gold yields to recover in Q1 FY27 toward Q2 FY26 levels (Q4 gold yield fell about 12 bps YoY, optically 28 bps); opex/assets already fell to 5.5% from 5.9% a year ago.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 148 gold branches opened in FY26 (34 in Q4) and further gold branch expansion is planned for FY27; gold AUM is INR10,352 crore (+76% YoY) with average AUM per branch at INR16.5 crore versus INR60-65 crore capacity per branch.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM growth guidance of 20-25% reiterated for FY27 with AUM at INR20,153 crore (+27% YoY); Q4 gold disbursals INR10,744 crore (+135% YoY) and about 60,000 new customers added in Q4, with gold tonnage budgeted at 10-15% growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed; branch expansion is funded from existing operations and the company's 22.4% CRAR is comfortable, though leverage rose to 4.6x, so a formal capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management could beat the 20-25% AUM guide if gold prices hold, since flat prices still allow 20-22% gold AUM growth and gold disbursals rose 135% YoY, but guidance was held rather than raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: A 10-15% gold price fall would test growth and ticket size (average ticket rose from INR1.5 lakh to INR2.6-2.7 lakh), leverage is 4.6x with about 25% of borrowings fixed, and stress is expected to lag in the affordable segment.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or brand launch was discussed; the call covers existing gold, LAP and co-lending lines.

rows.label: Credit cost range-bound and ROA up 20-30 bps in FY27
rows.why: Credit cost was 0.8% in FY26 versus 1.7% in FY25 and GNPA fell to 1.9% (from 2.0% a year ago); management targets ROA of 20-30 bps above the FY26 average, with a similar path in FY28.

rows.label: Gold yield recovery in Q1 FY27
rows.why: Gold yields fell about 12 bps YoY on back-ended disbursals and a 5-10 bps deliberate cut, with recovery toward Q2 FY26 levels contingent on competition staying steady.

rows.label: Leverage and borrowing costs
rows.why: Leverage rose to 4.6x from 4.0x in December 2025, and only about 25% of borrowings are fixed (30-35% including CP), so rising rates would pressure spreads.

tone.note: Management was confident on gold growth, asset quality and the ST LAP recovery, but cautious on rates and geopolitics; analysts pressed on gold yield softening, the ST LAP book's profitability (declined to give), and the FY27 ROA path.
